clue.text: Fixed a company's return after everyone gets shares

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed after the word for everyone

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: return tells us to read the fixed-a-company sequence backwards

parts.note: fixed means set, as in set in place
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A business report: a firm's financial return is settled once everyone receives their shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' gives OCATES. 'shares' is a verb here, not company stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To allocate is to distribute portions, which is what someone who shares out does.

clue.text: Slow movement, with nation confused

parts.note: with can mean and, joining two things

indicators.note: confused signals that the letters of nation are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A political lament: a country slowly moving forward amid confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' gives ANTINO. 'Slow movement' sounds like traffic but is music.
explanation.definitionFit: An andantino is a musical piece or passage at a moderately slow tempo, a slow movement.

clue.text: Free energy engaging Kelvin's observation

indicators.note: engaging means taking in, so the free-energy letters hold the Kelvin letter

parts.note: free means loose, unconfined
K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics remark: Lord Kelvin's observation about free energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' means holding, so the kelvin symbol sits within the free-energy letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look or inspection, an observation.

clue.text: Going ahead without precipitate assessment?

parts.note: precipitate looks like 'hasty', but as a noun it suggests rainfall: proceeding without checking the weather forecast, whatever it brings

explanation.surface: Pressing on without a hasty evaluation of the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitate' reads as an adjective meaning rash, but it hides precipitation, rain; going ahead regardless of the weather is the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means regardless of the weather, or more broadly whatever happens.

clue.text: Very large bird, a kind without tail

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: without tail means the last letter of the word for kind is dropped

parts.note: kind means nice

explanation.surface: A description of an enormous bird, of a sort that lacks a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE loses its last letter to give NIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, from the Titans of Greek myth, so huge in size.

clue.text: Right to support very good petition

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: so, as an expression of assent, can mean very good, fine
licit means lawful, right

explanation.surface: A petition claiming a right to back something very good.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to support' puts LICIT below SO.
explanation.definitionFit: To petition is to ask formally for something, which is to solicit it; both are verbs.

clue.text: Unresponsive having swallowed cold coffee

indicators.note: having swallowed means the deaf letters take the cold letter inside

parts.note: deaf, as in deaf to appeals, means unresponsive
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone unresponsive after gulping down cold coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside DEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaf is decaffeinated coffee, a kind of the drink.

clue.text: Arrangement of Abbey Road rightly overlooking a ridiculously high cost

indicators.note: an arrangement re-orders things, so these letters are rearranged
overlooking means leaving out, so the letter a is dropped from the pool

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement of the Beatles' Abbey Road, rightly criticised as absurdly expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement of' shuffles ABBEY ROAD RIGHTLY, and 'overlooking' leaves out the A. Abbey Road is the Beatles album named after the London studio street.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight robbery is a British idiom for being blatantly overcharged.

clue.text: Sound of fire? Expert heads for lifesaving equipment

parts.note: crack means expert, as in a crack shot

indicators.note: heads for takes the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: A firefighting scene: an expert reaches for the lifesaving gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is the snapping noise burning wood makes, so a sound typical of a fire.

clue.text: France a long time getting refrigerant

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: France spends ages acquiring a refrigerant gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Freon is a trade name for CFC gases once widely used as coolants in fridges.

clue.text: Work at arrangement to dismiss fine undervalued worker

parts.note: to do is to work or perform

indicators.note: to dismiss means to send away, so the fine letter is removed

parts.note: a format is an arrangement or layout
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An underappreciated employee is told to work at layout without being fined.
explanation.walkthrough: FORMAT loses F to give ORMAT; 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a person who lets others walk over them, someone used and unappreciated.

clue.text: Expose unprofessional lawyers before end of case

indicators.note: the lawyers come before the last letter of case

parts.note: lay means not belonging to a profession, amateur
the bar is the collective term for barristers

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of case

explanation.surface: Amateur lawyers expose things before a court case closes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay bare is to reveal or uncover something completely.

clue.text: Reckons pinching wrinkles — to reveal someone elderly?

indicators.note: wrinkles as a verb means creases or rumples, so these letters are crumpled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a pinch shows up wrinkles and so reveals an old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrinkles' looks like a noun about ageing skin, but it is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: No spring chicken is an idiom for a person who is no longer young.

clue.text: Revolting tribesmen turned in after murder

indicators.note: the turned word is placed after the slang for murder

parts.note: to ice is slang for to kill

indicators.note: turned means the word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: Rebellious tribesmen give themselves up after a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' means rebelling: the Iceni were the British tribe that revolted under Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe that rose against Roman rule.

clue.text: Collection at church — male put in a small amount of money

indicators.note: put in means the at-church-male letters are placed inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value

explanation.surface: The church collection: a man drops in a few coins.
explanation.walkthrough: ATCHM goes inside CENT after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchment is the act or area of collecting, as of rainwater or pupils.

clue.text: Interpret summary of annoying announcement at station I missed

indicators.note: missed means left out, so the letter I is dropped

parts.words: summary of annoying announcement at station
parts.note: a station announcer's bad news boils down to 'train's late'

explanation.surface: A commuter gives the gist of an irritating platform announcement they didn't catch.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIN'S LATE without its I.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to render words in another language, which is to interpret them.

clue.text: Enjoying the open air, excel around stables, perhaps, leaving husband

parts.note: to outdo is to surpass, to excel

indicators.note: leaving means going away from, so the husband letter departs

parts.note: horsy describes someone fond of horses, at home around stables

explanation.surface: A lover of fresh air does brilliantly around stables after a husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: HORSY loses H to give ORSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoorsy describes a person who loves being outside and outdoor pursuits.

clue.text: Quantity of liquid — a way to support place for fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits below, so it comes after

parts.note: a fish tank is where fish are kept
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A volume of water, and a way of propping up an aquarium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' in a down entry puts the second part below the first; the definition is a tankard-full.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is a beer mug, and by extension the amount of drink it holds.

clue.text: High part of building frequently involved in unskilled climbing

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the frequently letters go within
climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: poor means of low quality, unskilled
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A clumsy climber frequently ends up on the top of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the unskilled word upwards as ROOP, and 'involved in' puts the frequently word within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftop is the top outer surface of a building, its highest part.

clue.text: Solver to prohibit including river from West Africa?

indicators.note: including means the solver-and-ban letters take the river letter inside

parts.note: the solver is addressed as you
to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: A solver bans something from a river in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts the river letter inside the solver's word; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yoruba are a major people of Nigeria and Benin; Yoruban means relating to them, so West African.

clue.text: European wine European certainly associated with Spanish river

indicators.note: associated with places the two pieces side by side

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river
ja is German and Dutch for yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A European wine linked with a river in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Very lucky gent finally occupying working toilet

parts.note: on means working, functioning

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the final letters go within

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A fortunate gentleman finally gets into a working lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of lucky and gent, and 'occupying' seats them within the toilet word.
explanation.definitionFit: Only too, as in 'only too pleased', is an intensifying phrase meaning extremely.

clue.text: Queen's sad reflection on insular British, out of time, out of place

indicators.note: out of place means disordered, so these letters are rearranged
out of means without, so the time letter is removed from the pool

explanation.surface: The Queen musing sadly about island-minded British people who are behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' shuffles ON INSULAR BRITISH, and 'out of' first removes the T. The late Queen used the Latin phrase in 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Annus horribilis, Latin for horrible year, was Elizabeth II's rueful description of 1992.

clue.text: Father knocked over china in shock

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the word for father is turned round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
china means pal in Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate

explanation.surface: A father knocks over the china, shocking everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' looks like crockery; it is rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to horrify or dismay someone, to shock them.

clue.text: Player: one is found in orchestral area

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the one-is letters go within

parts.note: the orchestra pit is where a theatre orchestra plays
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A musician, one of many in the orchestra's space.
explanation.walkthrough: ANIS goes inside PIT after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pianist is someone who plays the piano, a musical player.

clue.text: Complaint by players dismissing latest nourishing drink

parts.note: beef is slang for a grievance

indicators.note: dismissing latest means the final letter of the word for players is dropped

parts.note: a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Players grumble after the latest batsman is out, then take a restorative drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM loses its last letter to give TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef tea is a broth made from beef, once given to invalids for nourishment.

clue.text: Liberal upset, say, with party meeting-place

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the say-and-party letters are reversed

parts.note: eg (for example) is what 'say' means
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Liberal, upset, perhaps, joins a party at its meeting hall.
explanation.walkthrough: EG+DO reversed gives ODGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodge is a meeting place for members of a society such as the Freemasons.

clue.text: Criticise that group of people about variable tights

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: about means around, so the those letters surround the variable

parts.note: those refers to a group of people
Y is a mathematical variable

explanation.surface: Mocking a group of people for their changeable taste in hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: Y goes inside THOSE after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantyhose is the American word for women's sheer tights.
